label: EdgeSwitch 10X
description: EdgeSwitch 10X (ES-10X) - 8x 1G RJ45 + 2x 1G SFP, 20 Gbps switching capacity. PoE passthrough only: it can be powered over 24 V passive PoE and hand it on; it does not source power on its data ports.
notes: Ubiquiti's own copy for this SKU describes PoE *passthrough*, not PoE output: the store and tech-spec metadata read "Cost-effective WISP switch with (8) Gigabit RJ45 ports, (2) SFP ports, and PoE passthrough support", where the ES-10XP beside it reads "each equipped with a 24V passive PoE output". Until 2026-11-20 this entry carried `poeOut: true` with `poeOutClass: "PoE"` on all eight copper ports - eight 802.3af sources on a box the vendor says passes power through. The arithmetic refuses it too: the tech-spec table (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/es-10x, HTTP 200, 574,925 B, read 2026-11-20) gives "Power method: 24V DC, 1A power adapter (Included), 24V passive PoE" - a 24 W supply - against "Max. passive PoE wattage per port: 15W", which is 120 W if all eight ports sourced, and the ES-10XP's supply is the 2.5 A one for exactly that reason. The PoE interface row ("24V DC passive PoE (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)") states the pinout and no port count, so which port receives and which passes through is a question this entry does not answer and does not guess. So the eight source claims are gone, `poe-pse` is dropped (it means "can source power on its ports"), and `passive-poe` is kept: the box speaks 24 V passive PoE, it just does not originate it. What would settle the passthrough pair: a quick-start guide or datasheet naming the in/out ports - `https://dl.ui.com/ds/es-10x_ds.pdf` answers 302 to the tech-spec root (no datasheet is published for this SKU, while `udw_ds.pdf` on the same host answers 200 application/pdf) and `https://dl.ui.com/qig/es-10x.pdf` answers 302 likewise.
